Documented Record

April 15, 1904 Incorporation Evidence

This page presents direct documentary evidence tied to the 1905 Yearbook record and related source files in this library, including the corporation name clause, signer block, and date-place statement.

1905 Yearbook Text Evidence

Corporation Name Clause

"The name of the corporation hereby created shall be 'General Conference Corporation of Seventh-day Adventists.'"

Date and Place Clause

The instrument records signatures in "the City of Washington, District of Columbia" on "the fifteenth day of April, A.D. 1904."

Signer List in Record

James R. Scott, Harvey Edson Rogers, Daniel K. Nicola, Arthur G. Daniells, and Amos P. Needham.

These five were selected by Daniells in 1903 specifically because they were D.C. residents — a legal residency requirement for D.C. incorporators. Their appointment was based on legal necessity, not spiritual office. See the 1903 minutes below.

1903 Committee Minutes — Premeditated from the Start

October 22, 1903 — Sixtieth Meeting: The Corporation Is Voted

At the Sixtieth Meeting of the General Conference Committee, Washington D.C., 9:45 A.M., October 22, 1903, the committee voted to create the new D.C. corporation and named seven original incorporators. The following is the verbatim record:

“Inasmuch as the General Conference Association is a corporation of the State of Michigan, requiring that its meetings shall be held in that State, to great inconvenience, as the headquarters is now removed; and,—

“Inasmuch as the legal Foreign Mission Board is a corporation of New York, requiring its legal annual meetings to be held there; it is,—

“Voted, That the General Conference Committee be instructed to create a corporation under the laws of the District of Columbia, to transact the business heretofore attended to by the Foreign Mission Board and the General Conference Association; and,—

“Voted, That the Foreign Mission Board be wound up and its assets transferred to the new corporation; and further,—

“Voted, That so far as possible to arrange, the new corporation shall give its notes to replace the notes of the Gen. Conf. Ass’n., and that when the Michigan corporation lapses, its affairs be wound up.

“Voted, That the incorporators be the following, and that they be instructed to elect themselves a Board to hold over until the next General Conference: A.G.Daniells, W.A.Spicer, W.T.Bland, W.W.Prescott, S.N.Curtiss, J.S.Washburn, A.P.Needham.”

“Voted, That we request the General Conference Association of Michigan and the Foreign Mission Board of New York as rapidly as possible to transfer all of their assets and liabilities to the new corporation.”

— Sixtieth Meeting, General Conference Committee, Washington D.C., October 22, 1903
⇓ Download October 22, 1903 Minutes PDF

April 13, 1904 — Five of Seven Replaced for D.C. Residency

By April 1904, five of the seven original nominees were no longer D.C. residents. The October 22, 1903 vote was reconsidered. Of the original seven, only A.G. Daniells and A.P. Needham survived. W.A. Spicer, W.T. Bland, W.W. Prescott, S.N. Curtiss, and J.S. Washburn were dropped — replaced by J.R. Scott, H.E. Rogers, and D.K. Nicola, who were D.C. residents.

“Attention was called to the fact that the majority of those named as incorporators at the October meeting of the Committee are not now residents of the District of Columbia, as required by law.”

— GC Committee Minority Meeting, April 13, 1904

“VOTED, That inasmuch as the majority of the persons named in the action of October 22, 1903 are not now resident in the District of Columbia, we appoint A.G. Daniells, J.R. Scott, A.P. Needham, H.E. Rogers, D.K. Nicola as incorporators of the General Conference Corporation of Seventh-day Adventists.”

— GC Committee Minority Meeting, April 13, 1904 — signed A.G. Daniells, Chairman; W.A. Spicer, Secretary
⇓ Download April 1904 GC Committee Minutes PDF 📁 All GC Committee Minutes — Adventist Archives

This two-step documented record (October 1903 → April 1904) proves the incorporation structure was planned, approved, and in motion well before April 15, 1904. The final five signers were chosen for legal residency qualification — not spiritual office.

The Great Wheel — And Those Who Left Their Machines

“I awoke, and fell asleep the same night, and dreamed that my husband was trying to right matters in the church at Battle Creek. There was difficulty. There were two or three that thought they had wisdom to bring the church into good working order. They wished to rearrange the church, and then they said it would be free. These men and women had a machine of their own to work, but the machine of each was united with a larger machine. Every one must keep his or her hand employed on his or her own machine, and then the larger machinery worked beautifully and every revolution of the great wheel was exact and harmonious. If any neglected this machine which was connected with the great machinery, every revolution of the large wheel made a disagreeable noise which disturbed not only the building it was in, but the building across the road jarred and shook.”

— Ellen G. White • 1SAT 1.4 • Ms. 1, 1873

“I saw two in particular leave their machines and [they] were watching the large wheel in the great machinery and were seeking to correct the great wheel, to have it more harmoniously and regularly. Instead of helping the difficulty, the machinery made a more disagreeable noise. I thought if all would stand by their own machines and diligently and faithfully do their own work correctly, there would be no trouble with the large machinery. But the noise of the large machine called the attention of several from their work. This difficulty was now to be settled. All wanted to know why the large machine ran so heavily, the wheel groaning at every revolution.”

— Ellen G. White • 1SAT 2.1 • Ms. 1, 1873

Written in 1873 about Battle Creek — thirty years before 1904. EGW describes the General Conference machinery: each man at his post, working his own machine, feeds the great wheel. The men who left their machines to “correct the great wheel” made the noise worse. The 1897–1904 GC leadership abandoned the pioneer prophetic post — they stopped proclaiming the Three Angels, the Sabbath, and the anti-papal testimony — and turned instead to building a corporate empire. The wheel groaned at every revolution. It groans still.

The Mayflower, 1620 — Fleeing the Church of England’s Persecuting Power

The Mayflower vs. the “New Rome”

In 1620, the Pilgrims aboard the Mayflower crossed the Atlantic to escape the persecuting power of the state church of England — an institution that used civil law to compel religious conformity and jailed, fined, and silenced those who dissented. America was founded on the revolutionary idea that no government may dictate faith.

On April 15, 1904, in Washington, District of Columbia — a city designed in the pattern of Rome, with its Capitol dome, its Obelisk, and its seat of empire — the same persecuting power the Pilgrims fled was quietly re-clothed in Protestant garb and registered as a corporation.

The “New Rome” issued articles of incorporation to a religious body. The church submitted. The state accepted. The union was consummated. The Image of the Papacy was formed — not by violence, but by paperwork.

⚠ The pioneers who built the Adventist movement on protest against Rome left their denominations when those denominations refused to reform. Their successors, just 60 years later, incorporated into the very system the pioneers had protested — right in the capital of “New Rome.” This is 1SM 204: “A new organization would be established.”

“The Reformers protested against the union of church and state. But the children of the Reformers have returned to Egypt. They build what their fathers pulled down. Heaven marks the movement: it is the image of the beast.”

— Alonzo T. Jones & E.J. Waggoner, 1888–1895, consistently

“In a union of Church and State the Church becomes MARRIED, as it were, to the State…”

— Ellen G. White, Letter 51a, 1898

Your great-grandparents' generation crossed an ocean and built a nation to escape exactly this.

The Pilgrims did not flee a foreign enemy. They fled their own church leadership — men who had taken the arm of the civil state and used it to silence, fine, imprison, and exile anyone who would not conform. They were not fighting pagans. They were fighting men who called themselves Christians, who wore robes, who held titles, and who had signed documents with civil governments giving those governments power over the consciences of the people. Sound familiar?

It should. Because it is the same pattern that was used against Jesus Himself. The Jews did not personally execute Christ — they brought Him to Rome. They went to the Roman civil authority, to Pilate, and demanded that the state enforce their religious verdict. “We have no king but Caesar” (John 19:15). They used civil power to kill the Son of God. His apostles were dragged before magistrates, imprisoned by the state, beheaded at Rome's command — all at the instigation of a religious leadership that had joined hands with the empire.

Do we think we are better than our Master? “The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.” (Matthew 10:24). The same Rome that crucified Christ is alive today. Its seat has moved — but its method has not. New Rome is the District of Columbia — laid out by a Freemason, its Capitol dome mirroring St. Peter's Basilica, its Washington Monument an Egyptian obelisk towering over Caesar's capital. And on April 15, 1904, a man entrusted to keep the faith sold out and hired signors — his hirelings — to sign the corporation papers in the District of Columbia. It was not the church as a body, but an apostate false shepherd wolf who betrayed the trust and led the flock into bondage.

On April 15, 1904, that same act was performed again — in Washington, D.C. — by men who called themselves Seventh-day Adventists. The Mayflower generation left everything to be free. Their spiritual heirs handed that freedom back — with a pen, in a corporation filing, to the government of Caesar's capital city.

If that does not wake you up, read it again.
